source.text: בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלְכ֛וּת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הָיָה֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] beginning of [the] reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, came the word this from with Yahweh, saying:

en.L: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying:
en.B: Early in the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:
en.R: When Jehoiakim son of Josiah had just become king of Judah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave this message:

decisions.choice: the beginning of the reign: the first months of Jehoiakim's rule, before his first full year
decisions.reason: The phrase names the time between a king coming to the throne and the start of his first full year as king (27:1; 28:1; 49:34). Jehoiakim was made king by Pharaoh Necho after his brother Jehoahaz was taken to Egypt (2 Kings 23:34), about 609 BC.

decisions.choice: this word: the temple sermon given in full in 7:1-15
decisions.reason: Chapter 7 gives the sermon at length; this chapter gives a short summary of it (verses 2-6) and tells what happened to Jeremiah after he preached it. The warning about Shiloh, the call to change their ways and the words "rising early and speaking" appear in both.

decisions.choice: chapter 26 of the Hebrew is chapter 33 of the Greek translation
decisions.reason: Because the Greek translation (the Septuagint) places the oracles against the nations after 25:13, this chapter stands later there (see 1:1). The Greek is also somewhat shorter in this chapter. The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: this word came from the LORD, saying: (L); this message came from the LORD: (B); the LORD gave this message (R)
decisions.reason: The heading is close to the one set for Jeremiah (7:1), and is worded the same way at each level.

decisions.choice: When Jehoiakim ... had just become king
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the beginning of the reign" means (m1).

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עֲמֹד֮ בַּחֲצַ֣ר בֵּית־יְהוָה֒ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֞ עַל־כָּל־עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה הַבָּאִים֙ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֣ת בֵּית־יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם אַל־תִּגְרַ֖ע דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: stand in [the] court of [the] house of Yahweh, and you will speak to all [the] cities of Judah the [ones] coming to bow down [at the] house of Yahweh all the words that I have commanded you to speak to them; not you hold back a word.

en.L: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Stand in the court of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and speak to all the cities of Judah who come to bow down [at] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all the words that I have commanded you to speak to them; do not hold back a word.
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Take your stand in the courtyard of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house and speak to the people of all the towns of Judah who come to worship at the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Tell them all the words I have commanded you to speak to them; do not hold back a single word.
en.R: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Go and stand in the courtyard of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. People from all the towns of Judah come there to worship. Tell them everything I have commanded you to say to them. Do not leave out even one word.

decisions.choice: stand in the court of the house of the LORD: the place of the sermon in 7:2
decisions.reason: In 7:2 Jeremiah is told to stand in the gate of the house of the LORD. The gate led into the court, and both name the place where the crowds of worshipers came in. The temple had more than one court (1 Kings 6:36; 2 Kings 21:5); this is one where the people gathered.

decisions.choice: all the cities of Judah: the people from every town of Judah
decisions.reason: The towns stand for the people who live in them. Crowds from the whole country came to the temple, most of all at the festivals, so Jeremiah would be heard by all Judah.

decisions.choice: do not hold back a word: say all of it, leaving nothing out
decisions.reason: The verb means to take away from or make less. The Law uses it for adding to or taking away from God's commands (Deuteronomy 4:2; 13:1). Jeremiah must not soften the message to protect himself.

decisions.choice: cities (L); towns (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word covers walled places of any size. Most places in Judah were small, so Balanced and Readable say "towns".

decisions.choice: People from all the towns of Judah come there to worship. Tell them ...
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long command into short sentences.

source.text: אוּלַ֣י יִשְׁמְע֔וּ וְיָשֻׁ֕בוּ אִ֖ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָרָעָ֑ה וְנִחַמְתִּ֣י אֶל־הָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֤י חֹשֵׁב֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָהֶ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Perhaps they will listen and turn each from his way the evil, and I will relent concerning the disaster that I [am] planning to do to them because of [the] evil of their deeds.

en.L: Perhaps they will listen and turn, each from his evil way, and I will relent concerning the disaster that I am planning to do to them because of the evil of their deeds.
en.B: Perhaps they will listen and each one will turn from his evil way. Then I will relent concerning the disaster I am planning to bring on them because of their evil deeds.
en.R: Maybe they will listen. Maybe each of them will stop living in evil ways. If they do, I will change my mind about the disaster I am planning to bring on them because of the evil things they have done.

decisions.choice: I will relent: God will turn back from the punishment he has announced if the people turn back from their evil
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God changing what he has said he will do, out of pity or in answer to repentance (18:7-10; Exodus 32:14; Jonah 3:10). His warning is not a fixed fate but a call to change. Verses 13 and 19 come back to the same word.

decisions.choice: evil way ... disaster ... evil deeds: one word for the people's wrong and for the harm it brings
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew word means both wickedness and disaster. If the people turn from their evil, God will turn from the evil he plans for them. The word comes back in verses 13 and 19.

decisions.choice: I am planning: the disaster is in God's mind but not yet carried out
decisions.reason: The participle describes something being planned now. God speaks as a potter shaping a plan that can still change (18:11).

decisions.choice: relent (L, B); change my mind (R)
decisions.reason: "Repent" would suggest God had done wrong. "Relent" and "change my mind" say that he holds back the punishment.

decisions.choice: bring on them
decisions.reason: Literally "to do to them"; Balanced uses the usual English phrase for causing a disaster.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אִם־לֹ֤א תִשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֵלַ֔י לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ בְּת֣וֹרָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִפְנֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will say to them, Thus says Yahweh: if not you listen to me to walk in my instruction that I have set before you,

en.L: And you will say to them, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: If you do not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, to walk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction that I have set before you,
en.B: Say to them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: If you will not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and walk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction, which I have set before you,
en.R: Tell them, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: You must listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching, which I have given you.

decisions.choice: if you do not listen ...: a condition that runs through verse 5 and is completed in verse 6
decisions.reason: Verses 4-6 are one sentence: if you do not listen to God and his prophets (4-5), then he will make this house like Shiloh (6).

decisions.choice: my instruction: all that God has taught his people, above all in the covenant law
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or direction. Here it is the covenant God gave at Sinai, which he "set before" them so that they could choose to keep it (9:12; Deuteronomy 4:8; 11:26).

decisions.choice: to walk in my instruction: to live by it
decisions.reason: Walking is a common picture for a way of life.

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); teaching (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Isaiah and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: You must listen to me ... (verse 6: If you do not ...)
decisions.reason: Readable states what God requires in verses 4-5 and puts the "if" in verse 6, to avoid one very long sentence.

source.text: לִשְׁמֹ֗עַ עַל־דִּבְרֵ֨י עֲבָדַ֣י הַנְּבִאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י שֹׁלֵ֣חַ אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְהַשְׁכֵּ֥ם וְשָׁלֹ֖חַ וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: to listen to [the] words of my servants the prophets whom I [am] sending to you, and rising early and sending, and not you have listened,

en.L: to listen to the words of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets, whom I am sending to you, rising early and sending [them], though you have not listened,
en.B: and listen to the words of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets, the ones I send you again and again, though you have not listened,
en.R: You must listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets. I have sent them to you over and over, but you have not listened to them.

decisions.choice: rising early and sending: sending again and again, without giving up
decisions.reason: As in 7:13, 25. To rise early is to start work at once and keep at it. God has sent prophet after prophet.

decisions.choice: my servants the prophets: those who served God by bringing his word
decisions.reason: As in 7:25, a title of honor for the prophets who spoke for God.

decisions.choice: though you have not listened: their past refusal, set against God's constant sending
decisions.reason: The last words change from "you" in the condition to a plain statement of fact: they have not listened so far. The question is whether they will listen now.

decisions.choice: rising early and sending (L); again and again (B); over and over (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase throughout Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: As in 7:25, "servant" is kept at every level when the word names those who serve God.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת־הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה וְאֶת־הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לִקְלָלָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and I will make the house this like Shiloh, and the city this I will make for a curse for all [the] nations of the earth.

en.L: then I will make this house like Shiloh, and this city I will make a curse for all the nations of the earth.'"
en.B: then I will make this house like Shiloh, and this city I will make a curse word for all the nations of the earth.'"
en.R: If you do not, I will make this temple like Shiloh. And all the nations of the earth will use the name of this city when they curse someone.'"

decisions.choice: like Shiloh: the first place of the LORD's worship, which he let be destroyed
decisions.reason: As in 7:12-14. The tabernacle and the ark were at Shiloh in the days of Eli, but because of the sins of the priests the ark was captured and Shiloh was left behind (1 Samuel 4; Psalm 78:60). God's house in Jerusalem was no more safe from judgment than his place in Shiloh had been.

decisions.choice: make this city a curse: its fate will be so terrible that other nations use its name in curses
decisions.reason: People would curse an enemy by wishing on him what happened to Jerusalem (24:9; 29:22; 2 Kings 22:19).

decisions.choice: this: the margin's reading of the word is followed
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text spells the word "this" with an extra final letter; the scribes noted in the margin the usual form to be read aloud. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: God's words to Jeremiah, and the message he is to give, end here
decisions.reason: God's speech began in verse 2, and the words Jeremiah is to say to the people in verse 4.

decisions.choice: a curse word
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the city's name becomes a word used in cursing; Readable spells this out (m2).

decisions.choice: If you do not
decisions.reason: Readable states the condition from verses 4-5 here (see verse 4).

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֛וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים וְהַנְּבִאִ֖ים וְכָל־הָעָ֑ם אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מְדַבֵּ֛ר אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard the priests and the prophets and all the people Jeremiah speaking the words these in [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And the priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The priests, the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speak these words in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The priests, the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah say these things in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah speaking these words: he did as he was told
decisions.reason: The narrator does not repeat the sermon. He tells only that Jeremiah delivered it, and goes on to the response.

decisions.choice: the priests and the prophets: those who served at the temple and claimed to speak for God there
decisions.reason: These prophets were the ones who promised the people peace and safety (6:13-14; 14:13-15; 23:16-17). Jeremiah's message threatened both their teaching and the temple they served.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀כְּכַלּ֣וֹת יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ לְדַבֵּר֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֑ם וַיִּתְפְּשׂ֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים וְהַנְּבִאִ֛ים וְכָל־הָעָ֥ם לֵאמֹ֖ר מ֥וֹת תָּמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as finished Jeremiah to speak all that commanded Yahweh to speak to all the people, and seized him the priests and the prophets and all the people, saying, Dying you will die.

en.L: And it was, when Jeremiah had finished speaking all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded [him] to speak to all the people, [that] the priests and the prophets and all the people seized him, saying, "You will surely die!
en.B: As soon as Jeremiah finished saying everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the prophets and all the people seized him and said, "You must die!
en.R: Jeremiah finished telling the people everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him to say. Then the priests, the prophets and all the people grabbed him. "You must die for this!" they said.

decisions.choice: you will surely die: a death sentence, made emphatic by the doubled verb
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated, "dying you will die", as in Genesis 2:17 and 1 Samuel 14:44; 22:16. They do not merely threaten him; they pronounce him guilty.

decisions.choice: they seized him: they charged him as a false prophet
decisions.reason: The Law said that a prophet who spoke in the LORD's name what the LORD had not commanded must die (Deuteronomy 18:20). The irony is that Jeremiah had spoken all the LORD "had commanded" him, as the verse says.

decisions.choice: all the people: the crowd at first joins the priests and prophets
decisions.reason: By verse 16 the people side with the officials against the priests and prophets. The crowd's mood changes as the case is heard.

decisions.choice: You will surely die! (L); You must die! (B); You must die for this! (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the doubled verb with "surely"; Balanced and Readable say it as a sentence pronounced on him.

source.text: מַדּוּעַ֩ נִבֵּ֨יתָ בְשֵׁם־יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ יִֽהְיֶה֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה וְהָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את תֶּחֱרַ֖ב מֵאֵ֣ין יוֹשֵׁ֑ב וַיִּקָּהֵ֧ל כָּל־הָעָ֛ם אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Why have you prophesied in [the] name of Yahweh, saying, Like Shiloh will be the house this, and the city this will be desolate, without inhabitant? And was gathered all the people to Jeremiah in [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: Why have you prophesied in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, 'This house will be like Shiloh, and this city will be desolate, without inhabitant'?" And all the people gathered around Jeremiah in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Why have you prophesied in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that this house will be like Shiloh and this city will lie in ruins with no one living in it?" And all the people crowded around Jeremiah in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: "Why do you say in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s name that this temple will be like Shiloh? Why do you say this city will be destroyed and no one will live here?" All the people crowded around Jeremiah in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

decisions.choice: prophesied in the name of the LORD: they deny that the LORD could say such a thing
decisions.reason: To speak in the LORD's name was to claim his authority. The priests and prophets cannot believe God would threaten his own house, so they treat Jeremiah's words as a false claim (Deuteronomy 18:20-22).

decisions.choice: desolate, without inhabitant: their summary of his message
decisions.reason: Verse 6 says the city will become a curse; the charge restates it in words Jeremiah uses elsewhere (4:7; 9:10). They give the gist of what he said.

decisions.choice: gathered around Jeremiah: the crowd pressed close around him
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean gathering to someone or against someone (Numbers 16:3). Here the crowd surrounds the prisoner, probably in a hostile mood (verse 8).

decisions.choice: two questions; the quotation opens again
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long question in two. Because its verse 8 closes the quotation after "they said", it opens it again here.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ׀שָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה אֵ֚ת הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַיַּעֲל֥וּ מִבֵּית־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּֽשְׁב֛וּ בְּפֶ֥תַח שַֽׁעַר־יְהוָ֖ה הֶחָדָֽשׁ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And heard [the] princes of Judah the things these, and they came up from [the] house of the king [to the] house of Yahweh, and they sat in [the] entrance of [the] gate of Yahweh the new.

en.L: And the princes of Judah heard these things, and they came up from the house of the king [to] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they sat at the entrance of the New Gate of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The officials of Judah heard about these things, and they came up from the royal palace to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house.
en.R: The leaders of Judah heard what was happening. So they went up from the king's palace to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. There they sat down at the entrance of the New Gate of the temple to hear the case.

decisions.choice: they came up from the king's palace: the palace stood below the temple
decisions.reason: The temple was on the highest part of the hill, north of and above the royal buildings, so one went "up" from the palace to the temple (36:10-12; 2 Kings 11:19 goes "down" the other way).

decisions.choice: they sat at the entrance of the gate: they met as a court to judge the case
decisions.reason: The gate was where elders and officials sat to hear cases and give judgment (Deuteronomy 21:19; Ruth 4:1-2; Amos 5:15). The king's officials take their seats to try Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: the New Gate of the LORD: a gate of the temple courts
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "the gate of the LORD, the new one". Some Hebrew manuscripts and the early translations have "the New Gate of the house of the LORD", as 36:10 does. The sense is the same: a gate of the temple, perhaps the upper gate built by Jotham (2 Kings 15:35).

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (1:18). These are the king's chief officers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: the New Gate of the LORD's house (B); the New Gate of the temple (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the gate belonged to the temple, as 36:10 puts it (m3).

decisions.choice: to hear the case
decisions.reason: Readable says why they sat at the gate (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְהַנְּבִאִים֙ אֶל־הַשָּׂרִ֔ים וְאֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר מִשְׁפַּט־מָ֨וֶת֙ לָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֤י נִבָּא֙ אֶל־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם בְּאָזְנֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the priests and the prophets to the princes and to all the people, saying, [A] sentence of death [is] for the man this, for he has prophesied against the city this, as you have heard with your ears.

en.L: And the priests and the prophets said to the princes and to all the people, saying, "A sentence of death [belongs] to this man, for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your [own] ears."
en.B: Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people, "This man ought to be condemned to death. He has prophesied against this city; you heard it with your own ears."
en.R: Then the priests and the prophets spoke to the leaders and all the people. "This man must be put to death!" they said. "He has prophesied against this city. You heard him yourselves!"

decisions.choice: a sentence of death belongs to this man: he is guilty of a crime that carries the death penalty
decisions.reason: The same words are used in the Law of a person who deserves to die (Deuteronomy 19:6; 21:22). The priests and prophets now bring the charge formally before the court.

decisions.choice: against this city: the charge names the city, not only the temple
decisions.reason: In verse 9 they spoke of the house and the city. Before the king's officials they stress the threat to the city, which made Jeremiah's words sound like treason against the state.

decisions.choice: you have heard: spoken to all those present
decisions.reason: The people had heard Jeremiah themselves (verse 7). The officials may have arrived later, but they are addressed with the crowd as one court.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (1:18). These are the king's chief officers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: ought to be condemned to death (B); must be put to death (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the legal phrase; verse 16 answers it with the same wording turned around.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־כָּל־הַשָּׂרִ֔ים וְאֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה שְׁלָחַ֗נִי לְהִנָּבֵ֞א אֶל־הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ וְאֶל־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁמַעְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeremiah to all the princes and to all the people, saying, Yahweh sent me to prophesy against the house this and against the city this all the words that you have heard.

en.L: And Jeremiah said to all the princes and to all the people, saying, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words that you have heard.
en.B: Then Jeremiah addressed all the officials and all the people: "It was {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who sent me to prophesy against this house and this city, to speak all the words you have heard.
en.R: Then Jeremiah spoke to all the leaders and all the people. "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sent me," he said. "He told me to prophesy against this temple and this city. He gave me all the words you have heard.

decisions.choice: The LORD sent me: the LORD's name stands first, for emphasis
decisions.reason: The charge was that he spoke in the LORD's name without being sent (verse 9). Jeremiah answers by putting the LORD first: it was the LORD who sent him.

decisions.choice: against this house and against this city: he names both, as he had
decisions.reason: Jeremiah does not take back any part of his message. He names the temple again, which the priests left out of their charge (verse 11).

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (1:18). These are the king's chief officers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: He told me ...; He gave me all the words
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence in two and repeats the subject. Sentence-initial "He" for God needs no setting span.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הֵיטִ֤יבוּ דַרְכֵיכֶם֙ וּמַ֣עַלְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְשִׁמְע֕וּ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְיִנָּחֵ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now make good your ways and your deeds and listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God, and will relent Yahweh concerning the disaster that he has spoken against you.

en.L: And now, make good your ways and your deeds, and listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will relent concerning the disaster that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken against you.
en.B: So now, change your ways and your actions for the better, and obey the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will relent concerning the disaster {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has pronounced against you.
en.R: So now, change the way you live and the things you do. Obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will change {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind about the disaster {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would bring on you.

decisions.choice: make good your ways and your deeds: the call of the temple sermon
decisions.reason: The same words are in 7:3, 5. Jeremiah's defense is to repeat his message: there is still time to change.

decisions.choice: listen to the voice of the LORD: obey him
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what they say (7:23; Deuteronomy 13:5).

decisions.choice: the LORD will relent: as God said in verse 3
decisions.reason: Jeremiah repeats what God told him: the disaster can still be turned back if the people turn back.

decisions.choice: make good your ways and your deeds (L); change your ways and your actions for the better (B); change the way you live and the things you do (R)
decisions.reason: As in 7:3.

decisions.choice: obey
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m2); Literal keeps "listen to the voice".

source.text: וַאֲנִ֖י הִנְנִ֣י בְיֶדְכֶ֑ם עֲשׂוּ־לִ֛י כַּטּ֥וֹב וְכַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, look, I [am] in your hand; do to me as the good and as the right in your eyes.

en.L: And I, look, I [am] in your hand; do to me as [is] good and as [is] right in your eyes.
en.B: As for me, look, I am in your power. Do to me what seems good and right in your eyes.
en.R: As for me, I am in your power. Do to me whatever you think is good and fair.

decisions.choice: in your hand: in your power, for you to decide what happens to me
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control (38:5; Genesis 16:6). Jeremiah does not resist the court.

decisions.choice: as is good and as is right in your eyes: as you judge best
decisions.reason: Jeremiah leaves the decision to them, but by speaking of what is good and right he reminds the judges that they must act justly.

decisions.choice: in your power
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "in your hand" (m1).

source.text: אַ֣ךְ׀יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּדְע֗וּ כִּ֣י אִם־מְמִתִ֣ים אַתֶּם֮ אֹתִי֒ כִּי־דָ֣ם נָקִ֗י אַתֶּם֙ נֹתְנִ֣ים עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֶל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את וְאֶל־יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ כִּ֣י בֶאֱמֶ֗ת שְׁלָחַ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם לְדַבֵּר֙ בְּאָזְנֵיכֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Only knowing know that if putting to death you [are] me, that blood innocent you [are] putting on yourselves and on the city this and on its inhabitants, for in truth has sent me Yahweh to you to speak in your ears all the words these.

en.L: Only know for certain that if you put me to death, you [will be] putting innocent blood on yourselves and on this city and on its inhabitants, for in truth {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to you to speak in your ears all these words."
en.B: But know this for certain: if you put me to death, you will bring the guilt of innocent blood on yourselves, on this city and on the people who live in it, for it is true that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent me to you to speak all these words for you to hear."
en.R: But you can be sure of this: If you kill me, you will be guilty of killing an innocent man. The guilt will fall on you, on this city and on everyone who lives in it. It is true! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} really did send me to you to tell you all these things."

decisions.choice: know for certain: the doubled verb makes it a solemn warning
decisions.reason: The verb "know" is repeated, "knowing you will know", to stress that they must not be mistaken about what they are doing.

decisions.choice: putting innocent blood on yourselves: taking on the guilt of killing an innocent person
decisions.reason: The blood of someone wrongly killed was thought of as resting on those responsible, and on the whole community, until God dealt with it (Deuteronomy 19:10; 21:8-9). Jeremiah's preaching named this very sin (7:6).

decisions.choice: in truth: it is really so
decisions.reason: Jeremiah answers the charge of verse 9. He is not a false prophet; the LORD truly sent him.

decisions.choice: to speak in your ears: to speak to you directly, so that you hear
decisions.reason: The phrase stresses that they themselves have heard the message (verse 11).

decisions.choice: the guilt of innocent blood (B); guilty of killing an innocent man (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture of blood on someone means (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הַשָּׂרִים֙ וְכָל־הָעָ֔ם אֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְאֶל־הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים אֵין־לָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ מִשְׁפַּט־מָ֔וֶת כִּ֗י בְּשֵׁ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the princes and all the people to the priests and to the prophets, There is not for the man this [a] sentence of death, for in [the] name of Yahweh our God he has spoken to us.

en.L: And the princes and all the people said to the priests and to the prophets, "There is no sentence of death for this man, for he has spoken to us in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."
en.B: Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man ought not to be condemned to death, for it is in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God that he has spoken to us."
en.R: Then the leaders and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man must not be put to death! He has spoken to us with the authority of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."

decisions.choice: the officials and all the people against the priests and the prophets: the crowd changes sides
decisions.reason: In verse 8 all the people joined the priests and prophets in seizing Jeremiah. Now they stand with the officials, and the priests and prophets are left alone in their charge.

decisions.choice: he has spoken in the name of the LORD our God: they accept that he may truly be the LORD's messenger
decisions.reason: The court turns the charge of verse 9 around. A prophet who speaks in the LORD's name must be heard (Deuteronomy 18:19), and they will not put him to death for it.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (1:18). These are the king's chief officers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: ought not to be condemned to death (B); must not be put to death (R)
decisions.reason: The verdict answers the charge of verse 11 in the same words.

decisions.choice: with the authority of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what speaking "in the name of" the LORD means.

source.text: וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים מִזִּקְנֵ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֶל־כָּל־קְהַ֥ל הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose men from [the] elders of the land and said to all [the] assembly of the people, saying,

en.L: And men from the elders of the land arose and said to all the assembly of the people, saying,
en.B: Then some of the elders of the land stood up and spoke to the whole assembly of the people:
en.R: Then some of the elders from the towns of Judah stood up and spoke to all the people gathered there. They said,

decisions.choice: the elders of the land: leaders of the families and towns of Judah
decisions.reason: Elders were the senior men who led their clans and towns and judged local cases (Deuteronomy 19:12; Ruth 4:2). They were not royal officers like the officials of verse 10, and they knew the history of the land.

decisions.choice: they arose: they stood up to speak before the court
decisions.reason: Standing up was the way to speak at an assembly or a trial (Deuteronomy 19:16; Micah 6:1).

decisions.choice: the assembly of the people: the whole crowd gathered at the gate
decisions.reason: The word means a gathering called together, here the people present at the hearing.

decisions.choice: from the towns of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the land" means here: the country around Jerusalem.

source.text: מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י הָיָ֣ה נִבָּ֔א בִּימֵ֖י חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־כָּל־עַם֩ יְהוּדָ֨ה לֵאמֹ֜ר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר׀יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת צִיּ֞וֹן שָׂדֶ֤ה תֵֽחָרֵשׁ֙ וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ עִיִּ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְהַ֥ר הַבַּ֖יִת לְבָמ֥וֹת יָֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: Micah the Morashtite was prophesying in [the] days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and he said to all [the] people of Judah, saying, Thus says Yahweh of hosts: Zion [as a] field will be plowed, and Jerusalem heaps of ruins will become, and [the] mountain of the house for high places of [a] forest.

en.L: "Micah the Morashtite was prophesying in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and he said to all the people of Judah, saying, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q Zion will be plowed [as] a field, \q and Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins, \q and the mountain of the house [will become] high places of a forest.'
en.B: "Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He said to all the people of Judah, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q Zion will be plowed as a field, \q Jerusalem will be a mound of ruins, \q and the mountain of the temple a wooded height.'
en.R: "Micah from the town of Moresheth was a prophet when Hezekiah was king of Judah. He told all the people of Judah, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q Zion will be plowed up like a field. \q Jerusalem will become a pile of ruins. \q The hill where the temple stands will be covered with trees and bushes.'

decisions.choice: the elders quote Micah 3:12
decisions.reason: The words from "Zion" on are Micah 3:12 almost word for word. In Micah the saying begins "Therefore, because of you", and the elders put "Thus says the LORD of hosts" before it; Micah also has a different spelling of the word for "heaps of ruins". Micah has not yet been translated in this project; when it is, the two passages should be compared.

decisions.choice: Micah the Morashtite: Micah from Moresheth, a town in the hill country southwest of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Micah 1:1 calls him the Morashtite, and Micah 1:14 names Moresheth-gath. He prophesied about a hundred years before Jeremiah, in the time of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah (Micah 1:1).

decisions.choice: Micah: the margin's reading of the name is followed
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has the longer form of the name, Micaiah; the scribes noted the shorter form Micah in the margin to be read aloud, as in Micah 1:1. It is the same man.

decisions.choice: the mountain of the house will be high places of a forest: the temple hill will be left to grow wild
decisions.reason: "The mountain of the house" is the hill on which the temple stood (Isaiah 2:2). "High places" here means heights or ridges, not shrines: the hill will be overgrown like wild country. Like Shiloh (verse 6), the place of the LORD's house can be left in ruins.

decisions.choice: Micah's saying is set in lines as poetry
decisions.reason: Micah 3:12 is a verse of poetry with three parallel lines: Zion, Jerusalem and the temple hill. The elders' own words are prose.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah (Isaiah 1:9) and through Jeremiah (7:3).

decisions.choice: of Moresheth (B); from the town of Moresheth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name his home town rather than use the word formed from it.

decisions.choice: the mountain of the temple (B); The hill where the temple stands (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which house is meant (m4).

source.text: הֶהָמֵ֣ת הֱ֠מִתֻהוּ חִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֜ה וְכָל־יְהוּדָ֗ה הֲלֹא֮ יָרֵ֣א אֶת־יְהוָה֒ וַיְחַל֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הָרָעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַאֲנַ֗חְנוּ עֹשִׂ֛ים רָעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה עַל־נַפְשׁוֹתֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Putting to death did they put him to death, Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah? Not [was he] fearing Yahweh and entreated [the] face of Yahweh, and relented Yahweh concerning the disaster that he had spoken against them? And we [are] doing [an] evil great against our lives.

en.L: Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah indeed put him to death? Did he not fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and entreat the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning the disaster that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken against them? But we are doing great evil against our own lives."
en.B: Did Hezekiah king of Judah, or all Judah with him, put him to death? Did Hezekiah not fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and plead for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s favor, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning the disaster {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had pronounced against them? We are about to bring a great disaster on ourselves!"
en.R: Did King Hezekiah or anyone else in Judah put Micah to death? No! Hezekiah respected {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be kind to them. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} changed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind and did not bring the disaster {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would bring on them. But we are about to bring a terrible disaster on ourselves!"

decisions.choice: did they indeed put him to death?: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. The elders' point is that Micah spoke words just as hard as Jeremiah's, and the king did not kill him.

decisions.choice: entreat the face of the LORD: plead with the LORD for his favor
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally to soften or soothe someone's face, to seek their kindness (Exodus 32:11; 1 Kings 13:6). Hezekiah turned to the LORD in prayer, as 2 Kings 19:14-19 and Isaiah 37:14-20 tell of a later crisis.

decisions.choice: the LORD relented: Micah's warning was not carried out in Hezekiah's day
decisions.reason: The elders take the fact that Jerusalem still stood as proof that God had answered Hezekiah's repentance, just as verse 3 says he would answer the people's (see 2 Chronicles 32:26). It does not mean that Micah's word was false.

decisions.choice: great evil against our lives: a great disaster on ourselves
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "disaster" earlier in the verse and in verses 3 and 13. To kill a true prophet would be a great wrong, and it would bring disaster on themselves. "Our lives" means "ourselves".

decisions.choice: the elders' speech ends here
decisions.reason: It began in verse 18.

decisions.choice: plead for the LORD's favor (B); begged him to be kind to them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m2).

decisions.choice: No! Hezekiah respected the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable answers the first question, as the elders mean it, and turns the second question into a statement. "Respected" gives the sense of fearing the LORD here: honoring him and doing what he says.

source.text: וְגַם־אִ֗ישׁ הָיָ֤ה מִתְנַבֵּא֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה אֽוּרִיָּ֨הוּ֙ בֶּֽן־שְׁמַעְיָ֔הוּ מִקִּרְיַ֖ת הַיְּעָרִ֑ים וַיִּנָּבֵ֞א עַל־הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ וְעַל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את כְּכֹ֖ל דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And also a man was prophesying in [the] name of Yahweh, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, and he prophesied against the city this and against the land this according to all [the] words of Jeremiah.

en.L: And also a man was prophesying in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, and he prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah.
en.B: Another man, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, was also prophesying in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Against this city and this land he prophesied words just like Jeremiah's.
en.R: There was another man who prophesied in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s name. His name was Uriah son of Shemaiah, and he came from the town of Kiriath-jearim. He gave the same kind of message against this city and this land that Jeremiah gave.

decisions.choice: and also a man was prophesying: the narrator adds a second case, which ended differently
alternatives: the speech of Jeremiah's opponents at the trial
decisions.reason: The elders' speech has ended (verse 19), and the narrator now tells what happened to another prophet with the same message. Some read these verses as words spoken at the trial by those who wanted Jeremiah dead, giving a case where a king did put a prophet to death, but nothing in the text marks a new speaker.

decisions.choice: Kiriath-jearim: a town about eight miles west of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: It was the town where the ark stayed for many years before David brought it to Jerusalem (1 Samuel 7:1-2; 2 Samuel 6:2).

decisions.choice: according to all the words of Jeremiah: with the same message as Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Uriah also warned that the city and the land would be destroyed.

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says that Kiriath-jearim is a town.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־יְ֠הוֹיָקִים וְכָל־גִּבּוֹרָ֤יו וְכָל־הַשָּׂרִים֙ אֶת־דְּבָרָ֔יו וַיְבַקֵּ֥שׁ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הֲמִית֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אוּרִיָּ֨הוּ֙ וַיִּרָ֔א וַיִּבְרַ֖ח וַיָּבֹ֥א מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard the king Jehoiakim and all his mighty men and all the princes his words, and sought the king to put him to death; and heard Uriah and was afraid and fled and went [to] Egypt.

en.L: And King Jehoiakim and all his mighty men and all the princes heard his words, and the king sought to put him to death; and Uriah heard [it], and he was afraid and fled and went [to] Egypt.
en.B: When King Jehoiakim and all his warriors and all the officials heard what he said, the king tried to have him put to death. But Uriah heard of it, and he was afraid and fled to Egypt.
en.R: King Jehoiakim, all his soldiers and all the leaders heard what Uriah said. So the king tried to have him killed. But Uriah found out about it. He was afraid, so he ran away to Egypt.

decisions.choice: his mighty men: the king's warriors, probably his officers and bodyguard
decisions.reason: The word means strong men or heroes, and often the trained fighting men who served a king (2 Samuel 23:8; 1 Kings 1:8).

decisions.choice: he fled to Egypt: Judah was under Egypt's rule at this time
decisions.reason: Pharaoh Necho had put Jehoiakim on the throne and made him pay tribute (2 Kings 23:34-35). Uriah fled to a land where he hoped to be out of reach, but the king's overlord could hand him back.

decisions.choice: the king sought to put him to death: he tried, but Uriah escaped for the time
decisions.reason: The verb "sought" describes the king's intention and the search, before verse 23 tells how he carried it out.

decisions.choice: mighty men (L); warriors (B); soldiers (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word's picture; Balanced and Readable say who these men were.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (see verse 10).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ יְהוֹיָקִ֛ים אֲנָשִׁ֖ים מִצְרָ֑יִם אֵ֣ת אֶלְנָתָ֧ן בֶּן־עַכְבּ֛וֹר וַאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אִתּ֖וֹ אֶל־מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Jehoiakim men [to] Egypt, Elnathan son of Achbor and men with him, to Egypt.

en.L: And King Jehoiakim sent men [to] Egypt, Elnathan son of Achbor and men with him, to Egypt.
en.B: But King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt: Elnathan son of Achbor and others with him went to Egypt.
en.R: But King Jehoiakim sent Elnathan son of Achbor and some other men to Egypt.

decisions.choice: Elnathan son of Achbor: one of Jehoiakim's officials
decisions.reason: His father Achbor was one of the men King Josiah sent to inquire about the book of the law (2 Kings 22:12). Elnathan is named again among the officials who heard Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll and who urged the king not to burn it (36:12, 25).

decisions.choice: Elnathan son of Achbor and men with him, to Egypt: part of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Greek translation is shorter here and does not name Elnathan. The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: to Egypt ... to Egypt: the place is named twice
decisions.reason: The sentence names the men sent and then repeats where they went, stressing how far the king would go to reach Uriah.

decisions.choice: went to Egypt (B); to Egypt said once (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps both mentions of Egypt in a natural sentence; Readable says it once.

source.text: וַיּוֹצִ֨יאוּ אֶת־אוּרִיָּ֜הוּ מִמִּצְרַ֗יִם וַיְבִאֻ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ יְהוֹיָקִ֔ים וַיַּכֵּ֖הוּ בֶּחָ֑רֶב וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ֙ אֶת־נִבְלָת֔וֹ אֶל־קִבְרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they brought out Uriah from Egypt and brought him to the king Jehoiakim, and he struck him with [the] sword and threw his corpse into [the] graves of [the] sons of the people.

en.L: And they brought Uriah out of Egypt and brought him to King Jehoiakim, and he struck him down with the sword and threw his corpse into the graves of the sons of the people.
en.B: They brought Uriah back from Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who struck him down with the sword and threw his body into the burial ground of the common people.
en.R: They brought Uriah back from Egypt to King Jehoiakim. The king had him killed with a sword. Then he had Uriah's body thrown into the graveyard for ordinary people.

decisions.choice: he struck him with the sword: the king had him executed
decisions.reason: The king is named as the one who struck him, whether by his own hand or by his men's at his order; either way the act was his.

decisions.choice: the graves of the sons of the people: the common burial ground
decisions.reason: "Sons of the people" means ordinary people. A prophet who spoke in the LORD's name was denied a family tomb and thrown among the common graves, as a mark of shame (2 Kings 23:6 speaks of the same burial ground in the Kidron Valley).

decisions.choice: had him killed; had Uriah's body thrown
decisions.reason: Readable says the king ordered it, since a king usually acted through his men (m1).

decisions.choice: the common people (B); ordinary people (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase is not a family name but means the ordinary people (m2).

source.text: אַ֗ךְ יַ֚ד אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן־שָׁפָ֔ן הָיְתָ֖ה אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ לְבִלְתִּ֛י תֵּת־אֹת֥וֹ בְיַד־הָעָ֖ם לַהֲמִיתֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Nevertheless, [the] hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so as not to give him into [the] hand of the people to put him to death.

en.L: Nevertheless, the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so as not to give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.
en.B: But Ahikam son of Shaphan stood behind Jeremiah, so Jeremiah was not given into the people's hands to be put to death.
en.R: But Ahikam son of Shaphan protected Jeremiah. So Jeremiah was not handed over to the people to be killed.

decisions.choice: the hand of Ahikam was with Jeremiah: Ahikam used his influence to protect him
decisions.reason: A person's hand being with someone means giving them support and help (1 Samuel 22:17; 2 Samuel 3:12). The verse sets Ahikam's hand against "the hand of the people": one protected, the other would have killed.

decisions.choice: Ahikam son of Shaphan: from a leading family of royal officials
decisions.reason: His father Shaphan was King Josiah's secretary, and Ahikam was one of those Josiah sent to inquire about the book of the law (2 Kings 22:12). Ahikam's son Gedaliah would later be made governor of Judah and look after Jeremiah (39:14; 40:5-6).

decisions.choice: nevertheless: unlike Uriah, Jeremiah was spared
decisions.reason: The small word sets Jeremiah's rescue against Uriah's death (verses 20-23). The danger had not passed with the verdict of verse 16; the people could still have killed him.

decisions.choice: stood behind (B); protected (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1); Literal keeps the picture of the hand.
